title: Ansel and the Bell
premise: Ansel Brightwater arrives in the fog-bound village of Hollowmere to teach at a school where children vanish from attendance registers without explanation, and he copes the only way he knows how: by writing everything down. He learns that the church bell, melted for scrap in 1911, still rings each dusk, and that every villager who once sang its last verse was bound to it forever. The missing children are not gone but kept, singing inside the bell's remembered bronze, sustained by a bargain the village founders made with something beneath the hill. In the end Ansel must choose between the woman he has come to love, who is already half-bell, and the duty of silence: he sings the verse wrong on purpose, shattering the song, freeing the children, and taking their place as the bell's new keeper until someone braver inherits his notebook.
about_author: Petra Whitlock is the pen name of a former parish archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing church records in coastal England before turning to fiction. She writes horror about paperwork, small towns, and the terrible intimacy of inherited obligations.

chapters.title: The Register of Small Absences
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Arriving in Hollowmere, Ansel begins teaching and notices names crossed out of the register in handwriting older than the ink around them. The villagers are warm but evasive; only Mara Voss, the sexton's daughter, meets his questions honestly. Emotional beat: quiet unease hardening into resolve as he starts his documentation notebook.

chapters.title: What Was Melted Still Rings
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with an interpolated 1911 ledger entry. At dusk the bell rings though the tower holds only air; Ansel climbs and finds scorch marks shaped like throats. Mara confesses her family has rung it for generations and that her mother now 'sings' somewhere below the hill. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Verse Beneath the Hill
chapters.summary: Ansel descends into the mine-shaft chapel where the villagers' bargain lives, finding the missing children mid-song, faces serene, mouths moving without sound. The thing below offers him a trade: sing the last verse and take Mara's place in her family's debt. Emotional beat: love against duty at full pressure.

chapters.title: Sung Wrong, On Purpose
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, closing with pages from his notebook left behind. He returns at dusk and deliberately mangles the final verse; the bell cracks through memory rather than metal, the children wake, and Mara is freed while Ansel's voice becomes the bell's. Emotional beat: sacrificial triumph shadowed by inheritance—the notebook waits for its next reader.
